goal: Tell apart mounting, labels and frames and what each does for a work on display.
note: Processes: present. Opener retrieval (ten minutes): the exhibit-plan card and work cards from year 1; reteach for a child new to the band. Free path: cereal-box mounts. Drawing or talk session: set-up 5 minutes, clean-up 4.

goal: Study Chinese paper-cutting hung for the Spring Festival on a work card: who makes it, where, when and what for.
note: Processes: connect, respond. Sensitivity: the sensitivity agent studies UNESCO's page on Chinese paper-cut first; no child imitates the tradition's designs; no child is asked to explain their own family's culture. Candidate kept (unit 12), no added day: both traditions' sources confirmed as the communities' own published teaching before the unit plan is written. Drawing or talk session: set-up 5 minutes, clean-up 4.

goal: Study Mexican papel picado hung for fiestas on a work card, and compare the two cultures' uses of cut paper.
note: Processes: connect, respond. Sensitivity: papel picado's use on Day of the Dead altars is a ceremonial use, named and studied by looking only (leave-out line on the course page); no child imitates the designs. Source: a Mexican cultural body's or a museum's page. Drawing or talk session: set-up 5 minutes, clean-up 4.

goal: Learn to group works around a shared theme for an exhibit by sorting sample works.
note: Processes: present. Drawing or talk session: set-up 5 minutes, clean-up 4.

goal: Practice matching a mount, a label and a frame to what each does, and sort sample works by theme.
note: Processes: present. Baseline look at the main look-for (the piece placed in its theme group and why it fits), not scored. Fold-in day on a year about 10 days short (into day 187); the baseline look moves with the drill. Drawing or talk session: set-up 5 minutes, clean-up 4.

goal: Choose the class theme, group the class's works on the exhibit-plan card, pick your own piece for a group, finishing one detail on it so it fits the theme, and tell who our exhibit is for and how it helps our school.
note: Processes: create, present, connect. Pr6.1 taught past the hook: the inside-school part (who the exhibit is for and how it helps our school). Drawing or talk session: set-up 5 minutes, clean-up 4.

goal: Mount, label and frame your piece and hold the critique with a partner: describe, ask, suggest.
note: Processes: create, present, respond. The unit's one critique. Glue sticks; hands washed. Drawing or talk session: set-up 5 minutes, clean-up 4.

goal: Revise the display after the critique and make the kept card matching a mount, a label and a frame to what each does.
note: Processes: present. The Pr5.1 kept card is made on the unit's last making day and scored with the showing. Drawing or talk session: set-up 5 minutes, clean-up 4.

goal: End-of-unit assessment, day 1: self-check, then talk items on how public art helps a community and how the two cut-paper uses compare.
note: Processes: present, connect. Pr6.1: one way Cloud Gate, a museum or the class exhibit helps a community (inside or outside school); Cn11.1: on the two work cards, one way alike and one way different, with where and when each is used; Pr5.1: the kept card, scored after the session. Response time: day 192. Drawing or talk session: set-up 5 minutes, clean-up 4.

goal: End-of-unit assessment, day 2: the year-end theme exhibit for families; each child says why the piece fits its group.
note: Processes: present. The showing is this unit's own assessment (after the year-end check, weeks 27 to 32). Pr4.1 guide look-for. Family yes for showing outside class; works under the child's chosen name. Drawing or talk session: set-up 5 minutes, clean-up 4.

goal: Second try at the part marked not yet, then a one-line reflection on the band's portfolio of twelve pieces.
note: Processes: present, connect. Groups from the record sheet. The folder goes home with a family note naming what grade 3 picks up. Drawing or talk session: set-up 5 minutes, clean-up 4.
